raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Forward-gathered parameters were not released when `stage3_max_reuse_distance` was set to a small value. The prefetcher skips parameters that are already available and records the step at which they will be needed next; the release path then retained those parameters until that step regardless of the configured reuse distance. Because the prefetcher can scan far enough ahead to see the backward reuse of parameters gathered in the forward pass, the parameters stayed resident until backward and accumulated across layers (see #7670).

The reuse-distance scan already keeps parameters that are reused within the configured window and releases the rest, so the extra prefetch-skip retention is removed in favor of that scan for non-offloaded parameters. `stage3_max_reuse_distance: 0` now releases parameters as soon as each module's forward completes and re-gathers them during backward, trading communication for lower forward memory. The trace scan also uses each future module's own leaf-module flag when collecting its parameters.

The prefetch-skip retention is deliberately kept for NVMe-offloaded parameters: releasing one also returns its swap-in buffer, and a later on-demand fetch can then fail with no available buffer. This preserves the previous NVMe queue/buffer ordering while keeping aggressive release for parameters that stay on the accelerator.

The default (`1e9`) behavior is unchanged: parameters are still kept resident through backward.

## Testing

- New `tests/unit/runtime/zero/test_zero3_forward_parameter_release.py` covers aggressive release with prefetch enabled (fails before this change), default retention, release with prefetch disabled, and an NVMe-offload training regression test (skipped when async-io is unavailable).
- Existing ZeRO-3 tests such as `test_zero_leaf_module.py`, `test_zero_allreduce_fetch_params.py`, `test_zero_context.py`, and `test_zeropp.py` pass on CPU.
- Manually validated with `torchrun --nproc_per_node=2`.
- `pre-commit` passes (flake8 run separately under Python 3.12).

Fixes #7670

+# Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+# DeepSpeed Team
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import deepspeed
+from deepspeed.ops.aio import AsyncIOBuilder
+from deepspeed.runtime.zero.partition_parameters import ZeroParamStatus
+from unit.common import DistributedTest
+
+
+class _TinyModel(torch.nn.Module):
+
+    def __init__(self, hidden_dim=16):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.a = torch.nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
+        self.b = torch.nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
+        self.c = torch.nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return self.c(self.b(self.a(x)))
+
+
+def _config(max_reuse_distance, prefetch_bucket_size=5e8):
+    return {
+        "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 1,
+        "zero_optimization": {
+            "stage": 3,
+            "stage3_max_reuse_distance": max_reuse_distance,
+            "stage3_prefetch_bucket_size": prefetch_bucket_size,
+            # Keep every parameter partitioned so the test observes release
+            # behavior instead of the persistence policy.
+            "stage3_param_persistence_threshold": 0,
+        },
+        "zero_allow_untested_optimizer": True,
+    }
+
+
+class TestZero3ForwardParameterRelease(DistributedTest):
+    world_size = 1
+
+    def _initialize(self, max_reuse_distance, prefetch_bucket_size=5e8):
+        model = _TinyModel()
+        engine, *_ = deepspeed.initialize(
+            model=model,
+            optimizer=torch.optim.SGD([p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad], lr=0.1),
+            model_parameters=model.parameters(),
+            config=_config(max_reuse_distance, prefetch_bucket_size),
+        )
+        return engine
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _run_to_complete_trace(engine, x):
+        # The first forward records the trace and the second one completes it.
+        for _ in range(2):
+            engine.backward(engine(x).sum())
+            engine.step()
+
+    def test_forward_params_are_released_when_reuse_distance_is_zero(self):
+        engine = self._initialize(max_reuse_distance=0)
+        x = torch.randn(2, 16)
+
+        self._run_to_complete_trace(engine, x)
+
+        # A completed trace would previously retain every forward-gathered
+        # parameter until its backward use because the prefetcher scanned far
+        # enough ahead to mark the reuse. `stage3_max_reuse_distance=0` must
+        # release them as soon as the forward of each module finishes.
+        engine(x)
+        for name, param in engine.module.named_parameters():
+            assert param.ds_status == ZeroParamStatus.NOT_AVAILABLE, \
+                f"{name} was not released after its forward use"
+
+    def test_forward_params_are_retained_with_large_reuse_distance(self):
+        engine = self._initialize(max_reuse_distance=1e9)
+        x = torch.randn(2, 16)
+
+        self._run_to_complete_trace(engine, x)
+
+        # With the default reuse distance the parameters are expected to stay
+        # resident through the backward pass instead of being re-gathered.
+        engine(x)
+        for name, param in engine.module.named_parameters():
+            assert param.ds_status == ZeroParamStatus.AVAILABLE, \
+                f"{name} was released despite a large reuse distance"
+
+    def test_forward_params_are_released_without_prefetch(self):
+        engine = self._initialize(max_reuse_distance=0, prefetch_bucket_size=0)
+        x = torch.randn(2, 16)
+
+        self._run_to_complete_trace(engine, x)
+
+        engine(x)
+        for name, param in engine.module.named_parameters():
+            assert param.ds_status == ZeroParamStatus.NOT_AVAILABLE, \
+                f"{name} was not released after its forward use"
+
+    def test_nvme_offload_trains_with_zero_reuse_distance(self, tmpdir):
+        # Releasing a prefetch-skipped NVMe parameter also returns its swap-in
+        # buffer. Do not regress the ordering that keeps the buffer count in
+        # sync with the trace, otherwise training fails intermittently with a
+        # "Not enough buffers" assertion in the partition swapper.
+        if not deepspeed.ops.__compatible_ops__[AsyncIOBuilder.NAME]:
+            pytest.skip("async-io is not available")
+
+        config = _config(max_reuse_distance=0)
+        config["zero_optimization"]["offload_param"] = {
+            "device": "nvme",
+            "nvme_path": str(tmpdir),
+        }
+
+        model = _TinyModel()
+        engine, *_ = deepspeed.initialize(
+            model=model,
+            optimizer=torch.optim.SGD([p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad], lr=0.1),
+            model_parameters=model.parameters(),
+            config=config,
+        )
+        x = torch.randn(2, 16, device=engine.device)
+
+        self._run_to_complete_trace(engine, x)
+        engine.backward(engine(x).sum())
+        engine.step()
